clue.text: Faces sanctions

definitions.meaning: faces are the features or visages of people
to sanction something is to approve or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A government confronting a round of international penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Faces are visages, a synonym; to countenance is also to permit or approve, as sanctions does as a verb.

clue.text: Leads may end in a scroll emendation

indicators.note: an emendation is a correction that alters text, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: Editing a scroll may finish with some corrections in the lead lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emendation' rearranges A SCROLL; a dog's lead ends at its neckband.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog lead clips at its far end to a neckband, so leads end in these.

clue.text: Frees oxen — or separates egg-whites, we hear

indicators.note: the answer is a sound-alike of words for separating whites from the rest of an egg

parts.note: removing the yolks could be called un-yolking

explanation.surface: A farmer releases oxen, or a cook separates eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns an invented word for taking yolks out of eggs into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To release oxen from a wooden harness pairing them is to take it off them.

clue.text: State of the river

definitions.meaning: a US state
a major river of the southeastern US shares the name

explanation.surface: Asking about the condition of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state takes its name from a large river flowing through it.

clue.text: Dropped by snobs — what'd'ye-call-'em?

definitions.meaning: snobs drop the identities of famous people they claim to know
a what-d'ye-call-'em stands in for the words we use to refer to things

explanation.surface: Snobs dropping the word whatsit.
explanation.definitionFit: Name-dropping is a snob's habit; 'what-d'ye-call-'em' is said when the label for something escapes you.

clue.text: Two essential items and the object of the game

definitions.text: Two essential items and the object of the game

parts.words: Two essential items and the object of the game
parts.note: the sport is named after its two necessary items of kit, a hoop with mesh and the sphere thrown into it

explanation.surface: A list of what you need to play a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The game's name joins its two essential pieces of equipment: the mesh hoop and the thing thrown through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A women's team sport takes its name from the hoop's mesh and the sphere thrown through it.

clue.text: Military formation makes the grade in other organizations

definitions.meaning: a stepped arrangement of troops, ships or aircraft
a level or rank in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: A military unit ranks well in other bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepped formation of troops is named the same as a rank or level in a company's hierarchy.

clue.text: It put Smith, that mighty man, in the shade

definitions.text: It put Smith, that mighty man, in the shade

parts.words: It put Smith, that mighty man, in the shade
parts.note: Longfellow's Village Blacksmith stands under a spreading tree, and 'the smith, a mighty man is he'

explanation.surface: Someone named Smith outshone by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in the shade' seems to mean outclass, but the smith of Longfellow's poem works under a tree's shade.
explanation.definitionFit: In Longfellow's poem the smithy stands beneath a spreading tree of this kind.

clue.text: Fabulous bird ? Happy days !

definitions.meaning: a bird of fable, the kingfisher said to calm the seas while nesting
a peaceful, golden time of life, as in the idiom for such days

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's exclamation of delight at a rare sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition stands for the adjective in the stock phrase for a calm, happy period of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend a kingfisher calmed winter seas while nesting, and the stock phrase for a past golden period uses the same word.

clue.text: Corresponds with red-heads sometimes

definitions.meaning: agrees with or tallies with
safety sticks for striking often have red tips

explanation.surface: Something tallies with people who have red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to tally or agree; a box of safety sticks for lighting fires often has red tips.

clue.text: Bird silenced by a Knight palely loitering?

definitions.text: Bird silenced by a Knight palely loitering

parts.words: Bird silenced by a Knight palely loitering
parts.note: Keats's La Belle Dame sans Merci has a pale knight where the reeds have withered and no birds sing

explanation.surface: A knight lurks pale and quiet, hushing a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In Keats's poem the knight loiters 'palely' where 'the sedge has withered from the lake, and no birds sing'; a songbird named for that plant is silenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reedbed songbird named for the waterside plant in Keats's line.

clue.text: Champagne effect, betting with a champion chaser

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in racing bets
Arkle was a famous Irish champion steeplechaser of the 1960s

explanation.surface: A punter celebrates a win on a top steeplechaser with bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: A chaser here is a steeplechase horse, not a drink after a spirit; Arkle won three Cheltenham Gold Cups.
explanation.definitionFit: The fizz and glitter of a bubbly wine is its effervescence, a glittering quality.

clue.text: Like the proverbial ox, prevaricated

definitions.meaning: Proverbs 15:17 speaks of a fattened ox kept in a stall
evaded and played for time

explanation.surface: Someone as stubborn as an ox, dodging the question.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Proverbs contrasts herbs with love against a stall-fattened ox with hatred; to delay evasively is to play for time.

clue.text: " Athwart men's—as they lie asleep:" (R. and J.)

definitions.text: " Athwart men's—as they lie asleep:" (R. and J.)

parts.words: " Athwart men's—as they lie asleep:" (R. and J.)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Mercutio's Queen Mab speech, where the fairy's coach drives over a sleeper's facial feature

explanation.surface: A quotation from Romeo and Juliet with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercutio says Queen Mab drives 'Athwart men's noses as they lie asleep'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The line names the part of the face the tiny fairy coach drives across.

clue.text: Ben's camel is odd in appearance

indicators.note: odd means strange, so these letters are taken in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A man named Ben owns a camel that looks peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the letters of BENSCAMEL; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward show or likeness, synonym of appearance.

clue.text: Severely hurt by strange tedium at start of Lent

indicators.note: strange means unusual, so these letters are taken in an unusual order
the start of the word Lent is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone suffering badly from boredom as Lent begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges TEDIUM with AT and L (from 'start of Lent'); 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be maimed or badly injured is to be severely hurt.

clue.text: Medicine ? Buy the chaps a drink, thickhead!

parts.note: to treat men is to buy the chaps a drink
the head of the word thick is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: A hangover sufferer told to stand his mates a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thickhead' looks like an insult but means the head (first letter) of 'thick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care for an illness is a synonym for medicine.

clue.text: For this one needs a ruler and a sheet of paper

definitions.meaning: a supreme sovereign of an empire
a large traditional paper size, 48 by 72 inches

explanation.surface: A geometry kit needs a ruler and a page to draw on.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of an empire is a sovereign; the same title names a very large size of drawing paper.

clue.text: Electric ray — the main weapon

definitions.meaning: a flat fish that can give an electric shock
main is the sea, and this weapon travels through it

explanation.surface: An electric ray being the principal arm of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief' but is the old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric ray is a fish also named after the self-propelled underwater missile, or vice versa.

clue.text: She's a game body full of colour

indicators.note: the governing body letters hold the colour inside them, as a vessel is full

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, governing body of the game

explanation.surface: A colourful woman who plays a sport with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a woman's name in the old style; 'full of' puts RED inside FA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a female, as 'She' indicates.

clue.text: Red in the face with a space-shot failing here?

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced because a rocket launch went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Canaveral, the US rocket launch site, is in this state, where failed launches happened.
explanation.definitionFit: The main US rocket launch site lies on this state's coast, so a failed launch occurs there.

clue.text: Stimulates — when we hear of former places?

indicators.note: the answer sounds like a phrase made from ex meaning former and sites meaning places

parts.note: ex means former and sites are places

explanation.surface: Something stirs us when we hear about places of old.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite is to stir up or arouse, a synonym of stimulate.

clue.text: News which should be heard

definitions.meaning: accounts of events
bangs or explosions, loud noises made to be heard

explanation.surface: News is something people ought to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts in the press are news items, and loud bangs from guns are also called by this word.

clue.text: The odd stray might be found in ancient woods

definitions.text: might be found in ancient woods

indicators.note: odd means peculiar, so the letters of the word stray are taken in a peculiar order

explanation.surface: A stray animal turns up now and then in old forests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges STRAY; the definition is descriptive: a woodland goat-man of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these goat-legged spirits roamed the forests, so one would be found in ancient woodland.

clue.text: One young in pride

parts.note: a pride is a group of big cats, and the young one is its baby

explanation.surface: A young person bursting with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' reads as self-esteem but is the collective noun for big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a lion group, so the young of the pride are its cubs.

clue.text: No trifling token

definitions.meaning: serious, not playful
a pledge or deposit given to seal a bargain

explanation.surface: A token that is no trivial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious means not trifling; money given in pledge of a bargain is an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Emblem included in Nicholas Nye's diet

definitions.text: Emblem included in Nicholas Nye's diet

parts.words: Emblem included in Nicholas Nye's diet
parts.note: Nicholas Nye is the donkey in Walter de la Mare's poem, and a donkey grazes on a prickly plant that is a national emblem

explanation.surface: A badge tucked into a menu for someone called Nicholas Nye.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Nye is a donkey in a Walter de la Mare poem; donkeys proverbially eat the prickly plant that is Scotland's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's national emblem is a prickly plant, and donkeys are said to eat it.

clue.text: Rum road races-very rum with these

definitions.text: Rum road races-very rum with these

indicators.note: rum means odd, so the letters of the first three words are made very odd, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Road races would be bizarre if armed military vehicles took part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very rum' rearranges RUMROADRACES; the first 'Rum' is fodder as well as part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured military vehicles taking part would make a road race strange indeed.
